title: Retriever Agent
description: Build a simple agent that answers from your own documents using vector retrieval.

setup.title: Get your project on disk
setup.description: Everything from here runs locally on your machine — the platform never hosts or executes your agent code. Lyzr only comes in at the very end, to actually run the agent you build.

levels.title: Root Agent
levels.desc: Bring agent.py to life and wire it to retrieval.

missions.title: Mission 1 — Bring the agent to life
missions.desc: The Chroma boilerplate is already wired up in chroma_setup.py — you don't touch that. Your job: pick the model and write the instruction it runs on.

miniSteps.label: Choose your model
miniSteps.sub: Flash vs Pro — a real trade-off, not a formality

miniSteps.label: Write the instruction
miniSteps.sub: What the agent is told to do on every call

missions.codeTemplate:
# imports + Chroma client are pre-wired in chroma_setup.py
from chroma_setup import retriever
from langchain.agents import create_agent

root_agent = create_agent(
    model={{model|tojson}},
    instructions={{instructions|tojson}},
    temperature={{temperature}},
    retriever=retriever  # ← from boilerplate, already connected
)

assist.tradeoffs:
gemini-2.5-flash: faster, cheaper, good for tool-routing.
gemini-2.5-pro: stronger reasoning, slower, better for ambiguous queries.
gpt-4o-mini: solid general default if you want an OpenAI-backed model instead.
assist.mistakes: Setting temperature above 0.5 for a factual retrieval agent tends to make it paraphrase away from the source text. Keep it low (0.0–0.3) for anything answer-from-documents.
assist.docs: See Lyzr Quickstart: Option C/D for how `provider`/`instructions` map directly onto agent creation params.

missions.title: Mission 2 — Wire the retriever behavior
missions.desc: Your agent already talks to Chroma through the boilerplate client. Now decide how it searches: which collection, and how many chunks it pulls back per query.

miniSteps.label: Name the collection
miniSteps.sub: Which Chroma collection this agent searches

miniSteps.label: Configure top_k
miniSteps.sub: How many chunks come back per query

assist.tradeoffs: Small top_k (3–5) keeps answers focused. Large top_k (10+) gives more coverage but dilutes relevance.
assist.mistakes: Setting top_k too high floods context and hurts answer quality. Most single-topic knowledge bases work well at 3–5.
assist.docs: See Lyzr docs: Agent Studio > Knowledge Base for how retrieval config is represented server-side.

finalize.goalTemplate: Answer questions accurately using retrieved context from the '{{collection}}' collection, top_k={{top_k}}.
finalize.testMessage: What can you help me with, based on the documents you have access to?
